To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) speakers of Valenciano Catalan contrast /lts/–/ls/, /rts/–/rs/, /mps/– /ms/ and /ntz/–/ns/, and (2) stop epenthesis occurs in /ls, ʎz, ɲz/ but not in /rs/.

1) speakers of Valenciano produce differently the clusters lts, ls, rts, rs, where /t/ may be underlying or epenthetically inserted and /l/ is underlying in /ls/; and 2) stop epenthesis applies in the sequences ms, ns, ls and ʎs with a phonetic realization that is robust in the two clusters with alveolopalatals and in /ns/ but absent or weak in /rs/.

the phonetic realization of the epenthetic stop in word final clusters with a nasal and /s/ is dependent on the segmental composition and the phonetic context of the cluster and that this realization varies across speakers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the phonetic implementation and the perceptual relevance of the phonologically conditioned deletion of oral stops in Valencian and other dialects of Spanish and Catalan.
the phonetic implementation of the epenthetic and underlying stop consonant in Valencian word final clusters and the factors that condition its prominence.
the phonetic implementation of epenthesis and its interaction with other processes, as well as with the role of phonetic implementation in the perception of epenthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Valencian Catalan has a complex and variable system of word final consonant clusters.

the epenthetic stop in Valencian is phonetically robust in /ʎs, s, ɲ/, and to some extent also in /ns/, but not in /ls/ and not at all in /rs/, while the underlying stops in /lts/–/rts/ are robust and the underlying stops in word final /ms, ns/ are phonetically absent.
the epenthetic stop is not phonologically present in /ms, ns/ but is present in /rs/, /ls/, and in /ʎs, ns/ to some extent, and is phonetically robust in /rs/, and in /ls, ʎns/.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Valencian Catalan speakers have developed a system where the phonological and phonetic implementation of word final clusters are more complex than the one in other Catalan dialects.
epenthetic stops are not phonologically robust, but that they may be phonetically robust in some contexts.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the phonetic implementation of epenthetic segments is a complex phenomenon that is sensitive to the phonetic and phonological context of the cluster and to the speaker's idiolect.
the epenthesis of an oral stop in word-final clusters is not always a phonetic phenomenon.
the presence of an underlying oral stop or stop epenthesis in word final consonant clusters may be reflected in the phonetic implementation of the cluster.
